name: Zilingo
one_liner: Fashion marketplace that pivoted into B2B supply-chain software and sourcing for Asian apparel makers

rounds.lead: Burda Principal Investments, Sequoia Capital India
Burda Principal Investments, Sofina, Sequoia Capital India

story: Zilingo started as a consumer fashion marketplace and pivoted to B2B software and sourcing for apparel makers, raising a $226M Series D in 2019 at a reported ~$970M valuation. In 2022 a fundraise surfaced questions about its accounting, CEO Ankiti Bose was suspended and then fired, a management buyout failed, and the company went into liquidation under creditors Varde and Indies Capital.

name: eFishery
one_liner: IoT fish feeders plus feed supply, financing and fish trading for Indonesian aquaculture farmers
story: eFishery sold automatic fish feeders and built feed, financing and fish-trading businesses for farmers, raising a $200M Series D in 2023 and reaching a reported $1.4B valuation. A whistleblower-triggered probe in late 2024 estimated management had inflated revenue by almost $600M in the nine months to September 2024 (about $752M reported vs about $157M actual), with two sets of books reportedly kept since 2018. In early 2025 it cut about 90% of staff while backers weighed liquidation, and an FTI report said investors might recover up to 10 cents on the dollar.

name: Investree
one_liner: Peer-to-peer lending marketplace funding working-capital and invoice loans for Indonesian SMEs
story: Investree matched lenders with Indonesian SMEs needing working-capital and invoice loans, and in October 2023 announced a ~$231M (EUR 220M) Series D anchored by Qatar's JTA International Holdings, structured through a joint venture. Regulator OJK revoked its licence on 21 October 2024 after it failed to meet the Rp 7.5B minimum-equity requirement and ignored warnings to inject capital and fix governance, sending it into liquidation. OJK then pursued ex-CEO Adrian Gunadi over alleged misuse of funds, and he was reportedly placed on Interpol's wanted list.

name: TaniHub
one_liner: Marketplace buying produce from smallholder farmers and supplying businesses, with a sister farmer-lending platform (TaniFund)
story: TaniHub bought produce directly from Indonesian farmers to sell to businesses and households, and ran TaniFund to lend to farmers. After the business wound down, prosecutors alleged irregularities and breaches of investment rules in about $25M of funding channelled into TaniHub and TaniFund between 2019 and 2023, and in 2025 arrested former CEO Ivan Arie Setiawan, a former board member and a former MDI Ventures CEO. Exact shutdown year and total funding are not confirmed by the sources collected.

name: Zenius Education
one_liner: Online video lessons and exam prep for Indonesian school students
story: Zenius was one of Indonesia's oldest online-learning brands for school students and scaled during the pandemic edtech boom. As the funding winter hit, it went through layoffs and in January 2024 said it would temporarily shut down operations, as reported in e27's roundup of the least-funded month of 2023. Funding totals are not confirmed by the sources collected.

name: Ula
one_liner: B2B wholesale app supplying stock and credit to small Indonesian mom-and-pop retailers
story: Ula supplied inventory to small warung shops through a B2B ordering app, one of several heavily funded Indonesian bets on digitising traditional retail. In 2023 it announced a temporary suspension of its business and then gradually shut down operations as the region's funding drought left thin-margin wholesale models unable to raise more. Funding totals are not confirmed by the sources collected.
